title: The Bridge Gives Way
text: The great bridge, older than any House, groans in the night and drops a span into the river. The divers sent down for the stones come up saying the river bed is full of hands.

temptation.label: Run your own ferry while the bridge is down.
temptation.text: There is a tidy profit in it, so long as the bridge stays down a while. Nobody need know whose ferries carry the trade.

triumph.text: The new span is finer than the old. Those who cross it keep their eyes ahead.

holds.text: Timber trestles carry the trade. The ferrymen charge double, and none will cross after dark.

falters.text: Trade dwindles. The empty piers fill with people who sit and stare at the water.

calamity.text: The river becomes a wall, and the markets starve. On still nights, hands can be heard knocking on the hulls from below.
